headline: A video company whose website finally moves like one.
was: The best story they have, that the studio started in a converted dog biscuit factory, sits on the About page instead of being the brand.
Services are spread across separate keyword pages like "Podcast production London", which read like SEO filler.
Search listings show a text-first site. For a video company, the work itself should be the first thing you see.

now.d: Six generated shots (golden hour, synth neon, studio spotlight, animation, bokeh, podcast waveform) hard-cut every 2.2 seconds with a flash frame, a changing slate and a rolling "We make …" line.
The bone logo fills as the reel counts to 100, then the screen opens like a letterbox. It plays once per visit.

now.t: A work index with a floating preview
now.d: Switch from grid to index and a preview follows your cursor across huge project titles, tilting with your speed.
Scroll down and five service reels slide sideways past you, with a red progress bar.
"Watch the showreel" plays a 5-4-3-2-1 film leader with a sweeping hand before handing you to Vimeo.
"Fetched." scrambles in, the marquee speeds up with your scroll, the story lights up word by word, the clapperboard snaps shut on submit, and the footer shows the time in London.

brand.body: The name was already brilliant. We just stopped hiding it. The logo is a dog bone with a red REC dot in the middle, so the factory story and the camera share one mark. Bunker black and biscuit gold do the heavy lifting, with a single hot red saved for anything that means record, play or act now.
points: A dog-bone mark with a REC dot: the story and the craft in one symbol
Archivo at its heaviest weight for headlines that read like title cards, and JetBrains Mono for timecode and technical detail
Voice: confident, a bit cheeky, and never corporate. "Got a brief? Throw us a bone."
A rule for every end card: the bone ident, then "Good content. Fetched."

marketing.idea: Make the studio's own channels the showreel.

plays.d: Turn every Vimeo project into its own page: the brief, the idea and the result. That ranks for "brand film for [sector]" searches in a way thin keyword pages rarely do.
A 60-second behind-the-scenes edit every month, cut in the new brand style. Agency producers hire people they've watched work.
A tin of dog biscuits sent to 30 target agency producers, with a QR code to the showreel on the lid. It's memorable, cheap and on brand.
Every podcast they produce gives three vertical clips for the client, which is also a free advert for Bunker's podcast service.
Claim "video production Shoreditch" with the showreel as the cover video and a project photo every week.

tierWhy: Creative agencies judge suppliers on taste. A full identity plus a multi-page site with case studies is the version that wins pitches.
